note: Generated by tools/gen-crypto-vectors.py. ACP-106 negative vectors: every entry is accepted by RFC 8032 as OpenSSL implements it, and MUST be refused by both implementations. Refused in Rust by crates/acp-crypto/tests/refused_ed25519.rs and in Python by the same generator's --check.

vectors.name: small_order_public_key_moves_1
vectors.why: The public key is the identity point, so `[k]A` vanishes and the equation stops mentioning the message.

vectors.name: small_order_public_key_moves_1000000
vectors.why: The SAME signature bytes as the vector above, over a message chosen to make the consequence plain. A verifier that accepts both has authenticated nothing.

vectors.name: r_is_the_identity_point
vectors.why: An honest key over an honest message, signed with `r = 0` so that `R` is small-order. The RFC 8032 equation genuinely holds; `verify_strict` refuses it anyway, and so must the Python guard.
